correctness.rationale: For a specified cyclic set of size c, a rooted forest has c n^(n-c-1) choices and its cyclic restriction has binom(c,k)D_(c-k) permutations with exactly k fixed loops. Divide by K~Bin(n,1/n) to obtain conditional law. Conditioning the k fixed identities makes each other site select uniformly among n−1 other vertices, yielding μ_k=k+sum_(j>=2)(n−k)_falling(j)/(n−1)^j. Falling-factorial differences show strict increasing finite differences; the two telescoping evaluations show μ_1<μ_0,μ_2, μ_2−μ_1=1/(n−1), and μ_0−μ_1 has Gaussian √(π/(2n)) limit. D1=0 makes tails at k+1 and k+2 cross with explicit positive and negative differences for 1<=k<=n−2. Conditioning a single fixed-point indicator and telescoping cyclic counts gives Cov(K,C)=0 exactly. Independent exhaustive exact rational mapping computations for n=3..5 confirm laws/mean/covariance, without replacing infinite proof.
residual_risks: The argument depends on the explicit stated hypotheses; no unproved extension is claimed.

evidence: Pitman, Forest volume decompositions and Abel–Cayley–Hurwitz multinomial expansions (Berkeley Statistics Technical Report 591 (2001)): Provides forest counts that are established ingredients, not the conditional fixed-loop regression or tail-crossing inequalities.

Hansen and Jaworski, Random mappings with a given number of cyclical points (Ars Combinatoria 94 (2010), 341–359): Conditions on number of cyclic vertices and investigates component sizes; opposite conditioning direction from C given K.

Hansen and Jaworski, A new random mapping model (arXiv:math/0603529): General random mapping distributions are related, but available statements do not establish strict convex K regression or zero covariance together.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Hansen–Jaworski general mapping enumeration covers counts of cyclic vertices and components, but conditional on C rather than on K; such reverse conditioning does not itself imply the claimed convexity or stochastic incomparability.

value.rationale: Number of cycles, cyclic vertices and fixed points are canonical statistics of uniform random mappings. Exact nonlinear and strictly convex conditional regression, sharp minimizer, stochastic-order crossings, and zero covariance reveal a nontrivial dependence invisible to first-order correlation; a natural probabilistic structural fact.
residual_risks: Mathematical significance is confined to the specified natural object and precise invariant; stronger generalizations are not asserted.

limitations: The conditional law is algebraically obtainable from classical exact enumeration; older authors may have recorded the same convexity or stochastic-order conclusions.
